solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Come to find photo frame empty?

definitions.meaning: to come to is to regain consciousness or recover one's senses
cryptically, the snap (photo) is no longer in the frame, so it is out of it

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a picture frame has lost its photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: a photo is a snap, and an empty frame means the snap is out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to and recovering one's wits after a daze are the same idea, an idiom for rousing oneself.

clue.text: Back-to-back rejections this time

parts.note: a no is a refusal or rejection

indicators.note: two rejections placed back to back, so the second one faces the other way

explanation.surface: Two refusals in a row arriving at this moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-to-back' sets two NOs against each other, the second turned round to read ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a specific hour, so it can be called 'this time' in a puzzle's playful sense.

clue.text: Sleep is interrupted by one returning: a nuisance

indicators.note: returning means the built word is read back to front
something interrupted has another thing break into its middle

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nap broken by someone coming back is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NIAP (I inside NAP) round.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling an irritating person or thing a pain is a common colloquial synonym for a nuisance.

clue.text: No good to cut down on consumption

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a phrase meaning consume a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Advice to consume less is dismissed as pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two for the second reading: use less.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless or ineffective is described as of no value, the plain dictionary sense.

clue.text: Round, round, round time after time he goes

indicators.note: the third round tells us the pair of Os goes around the rest

parts.note: each round is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A man going round and round again and again, like a merry-go-round.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same both ways, which the surface's endless circling hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name stands for any man, so the pronoun works as an example-style definition.

clue.text: All I found out about central pin is, it's crooked

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap about the other piece, which sits at their centre
found out suggests something discovered in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written
pins is colloquial for legs, so one pin is a leg

explanation.surface: A finding that a bent pin is behind it all, and it is dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' rearranges ALL I to ILAL; 'about central' puts LEG (a pin) in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked in the sense of dishonest or criminal matches something against the law.

clue.text: The — in dead-wood

parts.note: ash is a kind of tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the punctuation mark that joins the hyphenated 'dead-wood'.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed mark itself is the definition, and 'dead-wood' looks like one word but splits into D and ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed horizontal stroke is a punctuation mark whose name is the answer.

clue.text: Money made from big comeback?

parts.note: gross can mean big or fat
a return is a comeback

explanation.surface: Earnings from a big sporting or showbiz comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: Total income before deductions on an investment is a finance term for profit taken in.

clue.text: One has gone through much, to be honest

indicators.note: one piece passing through another ends up inside it

parts.note: far means much, as in far better
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who has been through a lot, speaking frankly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair dealing is just and above board, a synonym for being straight and truthful.

clue.text: Within moments, verdict of not guilty?

definitions.meaning: cryptically, an acquittal means the defendant serves no prison sentence

explanation.surface: A jury returns an acquittal almost instantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' is prison time in the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something done almost instantly, very swiftly indeed.

clue.text: Not that it's wrong to conceal an aspiration

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hide the other piece inside them
wrong suggests the letters are put in a wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written
H is the aspirate, the breathy sound in phonetics

explanation.surface: Denying it is mistaken to hide one's ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns IT'S into TIS, which hides H. 'Aspiration' looks like ambition but is the breathed sound H.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing to the near item rather than the far one is the opposite demonstrative pronoun.

clue.text: Nearly catching in button at rear?

definitions.meaning: just behind and about to overtake, in a race
cryptically, to button is to close and the rear is the behind

explanation.surface: A garment fastened at the back, nearly snagging.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes close as fasten and behind as the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuer just a short distance back and about to draw level is a racing idiom.

clue.text: 'One point' is constrained to become 'nil'

parts.note: N is one point of the compass, north
ought means is obliged or bound to

explanation.surface: A scoring decision where one point is forced down to zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero, the figure for nothing, is the same as a nil score.

clue.text: Only half listen, catching 'One's a predatory female'

indicators.note: catching means the first piece holds the second inside
half here means the first three of the six letters in listen

parts.note: taken as ones, the plural of one

explanation.surface: Someone half-listening overhears a warning about a man-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only half' of LISTEN is LIS, which surrounds ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: The female big cat is the one that does most of the hunting in a pride.

clue.text: Puts up with restrictive garments

definitions.meaning: puts up with someone as a guest, lodges or remains with

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates tight underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying with a host is lodging there, and corsets are traditionally called by the same word.

clue.text: Little beast requires meat: sitter doesn't have it

parts.note: ham is a cured meat

indicators.note: the word sitter loses the letters of the word it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet sitter refuses to provide the meat a small animal needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't have it' takes IT from SITTER, leaving STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent kept as a pet is a little animal, an example of the category.

clue.text: Undo buckles after hard part of hunt

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the other piece

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: buckles means bends out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unfastening buckles after a tough stretch of the chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckles' looks like straps but is the anagram verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox-hunting uses packs of dogs, so one dog is a member of the hunt.

clue.text: Gems — could be diamonds

definitions.meaning: excellent, dependable people, each called a real gem
in card games, any chosen suit outranking the others, which may be diamonds

explanation.surface: Precious stones that might be diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Gems looks like jewels but means good sorts, and diamonds is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A splendid fellow was once called a trump, so these are fine people; in bridge the winning suit.

clue.text: Upside-down sacks used as seat

indicators.note: in an across clue this means the word is turned round

parts.note: to sack a town is to loot it

explanation.surface: Inverted sacks used for sitting on.
explanation.definitionFit: A backless seat for one person is the plain dictionary sense.

clue.text: Is dispirited, having lost nucleus of savings

indicators.note: the core letters at the middle of savings are dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is depressed after losing the bulk of their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: The nucleus of SAVINGS is its middle three letters, VIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Drooping in spirits or flagging is a figurative sense of sinking down.

clue.text: Attack only when you say the word

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: An order to strike only on a spoken signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram with the head, as a goat does, is a form of attacking.

clue.text: Striving to put through levy, ingeniously

indicators.note: the answer runs through the inside of these words

explanation.surface: Struggling to get a tax passed by clever means.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing or contending with rivals is struggling for something, a synonym.

clue.text: Old soldiers taking part in running event

indicators.note: the soldiers enter the middle of the rearranged letters
running suggests movement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written
RA is the Royal Artillery, British army gunners

explanation.surface: Former servicemen joining in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldiers' wants to be the definition, but 'soldiers' is the Royal Artillery and 'Old' alone defines, as in a veteran car. 'running' scrambles EVENT to VETEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving or aged thing, such as a vintage car, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Pugs romping round animal: huge creature

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
romping dogs move about wildly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Little dogs frolicking around a much larger beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romping' scrambles the dogs into GPUS; 'animal' is deliberately vague, and here the male sheep fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampus is an old name for the killer whale or Risso's dolphin, a large sea mammal.

clue.text: Fights to be let out, imprisoned by lunatic

indicators.note: the second piece is locked inside the first

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner held by a madman fights to be freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the fodder to TLE; 'bats' as slang for crazy is the less obvious sense of 'lunatic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Battles and fights are synonyms for combats or struggles.

clue.text: One can't catch something in the dispensary

definitions.meaning: someone who keeps letting the ball fall, a fumbling fielder
a pipette for giving medicine drop by drop, found in a pharmacy

explanation.surface: A pharmacy item handled by someone with butterfingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lets things fall, and a glass tube for measuring out liquid medicine in drops.

clue.text: Is not penniless — is a catch

definitions.meaning: cryptically, ..., P being the abbreviation for a penny
a hinged fastening on a door or lid

explanation.surface: Someone with money is a desirable partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'not penniless' as 'has P', P being a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged metal fastening for a door or lid is a kind of latch.

clue.text: Locate one in heart of West End

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
only the heart is kept, so the outer letters of the phrase West End go

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Finding someone in the centre of London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is central London's theatre and shopping area; its heart gives STE.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to position or place it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ken's delivered from a naysayer

definitions.note: read as 'ken is', ken meaning be aware of

indicators.note: delivered in the sense of spoken, a speech delivered aloud

parts.note: someone who says nay says no

explanation.surface: A man called Ken has been rescued from a pessimist.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken looks like a name but is the Scottish word meaning to be aware; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken is the Scots verb for being acquainted with or understanding something.

clue.text: A time to plough up field

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A farmer picking a moment to till a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or expertise is a domain or zone, the same sense.

clue.text: Formerly addicted to coke, having kicked all right

parts.note: being on a drug means taking it habitually

indicators.note: kicking a habit means giving it up, so letters leave the word coke

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: An ex-cocaine user who has kicked the habit and is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having kicked' removes OK from COKE, leaving CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at one time in the past happened at a previous time, a synonym.

clue.text: Mean to be among entrants playing in Open

indicators.note: the mean piece goes in the midst of the rearranged letters
playing suggests the letters move about and are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written
par is the average or mean standard

explanation.surface: An average golfer among the competitors at the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like the golf tournament, but it is the definition, meaning frank. Par is golf's standard score, hence 'Mean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and frank behaviour with nothing hidden is clear for all to see through.

clue.text: Unbalanced, rock back

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock or stun them

explanation.surface: A boulder rolling back is precarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad or crazy, mentally disturbed.

clue.text: Quickly as stutterer starts answering 'Who wrote "Hamlet"?'

definitions.meaning: a stammerer replying with the playwright's name would begin with his first syllable said twice

explanation.surface: A stammerer hurriedly answering a literature quiz question.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutterer says 'Shakes... Shakes...' before getting to the name of the author of Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for very soon, as fast as a couple of jiggles of a lamb's tail.
